name: [Istio] Container OOMKilled — {{kube_namespace.name}}/{{kube_container_name.name}}
message:
:rotating_light: **{{kube_container_name.name}} was OOMKilled {{value}} time(s) in the last 15 minutes.**

Namespace: `{{kube_namespace.name}}`
Cluster: `{{kube_cluster_name.name}}`

This fires on the kill itself rather than on a threshold, so it is the ground truth for the saturation monitors — if this fires and the saturation monitor did not, the growth was faster than the 10-minute evaluation window and the thresholds need lowering or the window shortening.

**Triage**
1. `kubectl describe pod <pod> -n {{kube_namespace.name}}` and look for `Last State: Terminated, Reason: OOMKilled`.
2. Compare the memory graph immediately before the kill against the sustained baseline. A sharp spike points at a single large request or a burst of connections; a slow climb points at a leak or at config growth.
3. Raising the limit is the fix only if the baseline is legitimately above the limit. If it is a leak, a higher limit just moves the kill later.
